items.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: talking about the Jack Teagardens and Hackett and Benny Goodman. You know, really giant players, so many that you’d come across.

ctx.x: Somehow you wonder how you survived that, huh?

Well you didn’t hurt yourself, it was just fine. You know those days in New York, it was easy. You could go out at night. It wasn’t if you hung out at night or if you wound up in Harlem or as they say and things like that and visiting some of those clubs where you have to say I work with James P. Johnson and Willie Smith. My first job in New York, © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

when I came in there, they were playing two pianos in there. Maxie Kaminsky had just come back from with Artie Shaw’s band and he put a band together and it was Willie Smith and Rod Kless I remember, myself, and a couple of guys, and James P. Johnson and the Lion were the two pianos. They had a grand piano and an upright piano, and Willie played intermission and they would open at seven o’clock at night and they’d play ‘till five, six in the morning. And all these, you know, fantastic piano players would come in,…
